decan_list: Senenmut TT 353 (~1473 BCE), cross-checked with Dendera ceiling (~50 BCE) and Sety I tomb (~1290 BCE). Per Neugebauer & Parker EAT III.
ayanamsa: Lahiri (Chitrapaksha), ~24°10' for 2026 CE — Vedic Nakshatras given in sidereal degrees.
face_ruler_convention: Chaldean order Sa-Ju-Ma-Su-Ve-Me-Mo per Picatrix II.11 / Liber Hermetis / Agrippa III.18.
xiu_orientation: Dominant-star convention per Sun & Kistemaker 1997 Tables 8.1-8.3. Xiu numbering starts at 角 (Jiao, Spica/Virgo wing) which sits at ~22° Virgo tropical — so the cyclical offset must be tracked.
alignment_caveat: 36 decans (10°) vs 27/28 mansions (12.86°) do not tile evenly. Where a decan overlaps two mansions, dominant first; minor noted in caveat field. Nakshatras given in sidereal Lahiri; Manazil and Xiu in tropical/sidereal hybrid per their respective traditions.

western.picatrix_image: A tall dark restless man with red eyes, axe in hand, white-clothed; significations: boldness, daring, lordship.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Decanic tradition is directly Egyptian — Demotic + Greek decan-lists (Hermes Trismegistus corpus, ~2nd c. BCE) preserved through Roman Egypt into Arabic Harran (~9th c.) and thence Picatrix. Aśvinī/Sharaṭān/Lóu all anchor at Aries 0° by convention.

western.picatrix_image: A woman in green raiment, lacking one leg; significations: nobility, pride, exalted dominion.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix decan-2 image (one-legged woman) parallels Egyptian limping-deity motif (Horus injuring leg). Triplicity ruler unchanged through the sign.

western.picatrix_image: A restless man holding a golden bracelet, wearing red; significations: subtlety, cunning, lightness.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: MASSIVE CONVERGENCE — Al-Thurayyā = Mǎo = Kṛttikā all refer to the Pleiades; three independent traditions name the same star-cluster as a calendrical anchor. Aśvinī ends, Bharaṇī begins here (sidereal offset).

western.picatrix_image: A naked man, an archer, a harvester or husbandman; significations: ploughing, sowing, building, peopling, dividing the earth.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Aldebaran (Al-Dabarān = 'the follower [of Pleiades]') is the Hyades cluster's brightest star; Chinese Bì = Hyades + Aldebaran net-shape. Kṛttikā nakshatra crosses the Aries/Taurus boundary in Lahiri sidereal.

western.picatrix_image: A naked man holding a key; significations: power, nobility, rule over the people.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Rohiṇī (literally 'reddish') corresponds to Aldebaran — but Lahiri sidereal places it at 10°-23°20' Taurus, so it dominates Taurus decan 2. The Manzil-5 and Xiu-20 alignment shifts away from the zodiac belt to Orion's head — characteristic Manazil/Xiu drift.

western.picatrix_image: A man with a serpent in his hand, leading a horse; significations: idleness, but also dominion over flocks.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Mṛgaśīrṣa = 'deer-head' refers to Orion (the Chinese Shēn is Orion's belt + sword). Three traditions name Orion as a hunter / deer-figure. Manzil-6 (Al-Hanʿa) shifts to Gemini stars.
decans.caveat: Egyptian decan-6 deity attribution varies — some lists give Set/Sutekh, others Sopdet's adjacent. Uncertain.

western.picatrix_image: A beautiful woman holding a rod, well-clothed; significations: writing, computation, art.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix's beautiful-scribe image directly maps to Thoth (Egyptian writing-deity). Castor/Pollux (Al-Dhirāʿ) and Gemini-stars (Jǐng) all converge here. Vedic Ārdrā = α Orionis (Betelgeuse) — slight latitude offset from ecliptic.

western.picatrix_image: A man holding a flute, bent over; significations: ingenuity, dishonor, mockery.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: MASSIVE CONVERGENCE — Praesepe (the Beehive Cluster, M44) is named in three traditions: Al-Nathra (nose), Guǐ (ghost gathering), and Picatrix often associates this with hidden gatherings.

western.picatrix_image: A man wearing armor, holding a bow and arrows; significations: oblivion, contempt, jest, but also strong arms.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Egyptian 'middle of the boat' = solar barque imagery — Sun-face ruler reinforces this. Hydra head (Chinese Liǔ) and Cancer-Leo border (Manzil 9) shift away from the ecliptic.

western.picatrix_image: A man twisted, with the face of a horse, and the feet of an eagle, with a fig-tree before him; significations: subtlety, cleverness, mastery.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix horse-faced eagle-footed image preserves an explicit Egyptian-Greek hybrid (Greek decan-images in Liber Hermetis are very close to these). Sopdet (Sirius) rises near Cancer cusp in the Egyptian sky and marks the Nile flood — anchor for the entire Egyptian calendar.

western.picatrix_image: A beautiful woman, garlanded, holding a wand; significations: play, riches, joy, abundance.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix 'garlanded woman' parallels Isis-Hathor festival imagery. Cancer decan 2 is the most-fortunate decan in Picatrix face-rulership.

western.picatrix_image: A turtle-shaped man, or a man with a turtle in his hand; significations: swiftness in love, daring, oratory.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Aśleṣā ('embrace' / serpent) corresponds nicely to Picatrix's serpentine-water imagery (turtle as water-creature). End of Cancer = end of first quadrant in tropical zodiac.

western.picatrix_image: A man with a sword and a small shield, in red garments; significations: boldness, violence, cruelty, ferocity.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Sekhmet (lion-warrior) directly maps onto Leo decan 1's martial Picatrix imagery. Maghā nakshatra is the 'royal' nakshatra in Vedic tradition. End of Chinese Xiu cycle (28 → 1).

western.picatrix_image: A man on a horse, with a long beard and crowned with a laurel garland; significations: love, fellowship, profit.

vedic.symbol: hammock / front legs of a cot

decans.cross_tradition_notes: CYCLICAL ANCHOR — Spica = Al-Simāk = Jiǎo (the horn of the Azure Dragon). Chinese Xiu cycle restarts here at 角 (Jiǎo). This is the canonical 'beginning point' in the Chinese 28-mansion cycle even though zodiacally it sits late.

western.picatrix_image: A young man holding a whip, mournful and sad; significations: love, delight, but also flight and absence.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Uttara-Phalgunī ('latter red one') crosses Leo/Virgo border in sidereal. Manzil-15 and Xiu-2 align as the Virgo-arm group.

western.picatrix_image: A girl wearing white linen, with a pomegranate in her hand; significations: virginity, modesty, eloquence.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix girl-with-pomegranate is Persephone — direct Hellenistic syncretism with Greek Demeter cycle. The pre-Hellenistic zodiac had no Libra: Manzil-16 + Xiu-3 both still refer to Scorpio's claws (Zubānā = 'claws').

western.picatrix_image: A black man clothed in skins, a beard, holding a sack of money; significations: gain by labor, profit, harvest.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Citrā ('shining') = α Virginis (Spica). MASSIVE CONVERGENCE — Spica is the brightest star in this zodiacal stretch and shows up by name in multiple traditions.

western.picatrix_image: A white woman, deaf, lame, holding tablets; significations: virtue, weakness, journey.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: MASSIVE CONVERGENCE — Antares is 'heart' in three traditions: Al-Qalb (Arabic), Xīn (Chinese), Kardia (Greek 'Antares' = anti-Ares = rival of Mars, the heart of the Scorpion). Three traditions independently identified this red star as a thoracic anchor.

western.picatrix_image: An angry man holding a lance; significations: justice, judgment, dispute, anger.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Anubis weighs the heart in Egyptian judgment — Libra-justice imagery is post-Hellenistic Egyptian. The Scorpio sting (Shawla / Wěi) all sit in this decan-stretch.

western.picatrix_image: Two men in raiment, dancing, joined hand-to-hand; significations: joy, levity, the merry-go-round of life.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Indra-Agni (paired devas) → Picatrix 'two men joined hand-to-hand' is striking. Sagittarius-stars enter the Manzil and Xiu mapping here.
decans.caveat: Egyptian decan-20 deity attribution disputed across Senenmut/Dendera lists.

western.picatrix_image: A violent man with a bow, naked, blood-stained; significations: evil deeds, violence, but also vigilance.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Black Tortoise / Northern Palace begins at Xiu-8 (Dǒu). Manzil-21 is famously the 'empty quarter' between bright stars in Sagittarius — three traditions noting the relative emptiness here.

western.picatrix_image: A woman of beautiful form, scorpion-tailed; significations: sleep, idleness, love.

arabic_manzil.name: Saʿd al-Dhābih
arabic_manzil.translation: The Lucky One of the Slaughterer

decans.cross_tradition_notes: MASSIVE CONVERGENCE — Capricorn's horns = Niú (Ox horns) = Dhābih ('slaughterer' = sacrificial bull). Three traditions name this asterism as horned-cattle imagery.

western.picatrix_image: A man on a camel, with a scorpion in his hand; significations: knowledge, ferocity, deceit.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Aquarius-stars now enter the Manazil/Xiu cycle. Jyeṣṭhā = 'eldest' aligns with Indra in Vedic — paralleling Picatrix's 'man with camel' (camel = burden-bearer / patriarch).

western.picatrix_image: A horse and a wolf; significations: subtlety, plotting, wickedness.

arabic_manzil.name: Saʿd al-Suʿūd
arabic_manzil.stars: β Aquarii (Sadalsuud), ξ Aquarii, c Capricorni

decans.cross_tradition_notes: STRIKING INVERSION — same star (β Aquarii / Sadalsuud) is 'luckiest' in Arabic but 'void/empty' in Chinese. Demonstrates how positional naming carries opposite valences across cultures.

western.picatrix_image: A man armed with a coat-of-mail and a sword; significations: boldness, malice, valor.

arabic_manzil.name: Saʿd al-Akhbiya
arabic_manzil.translation: The Lucky One of the Tents

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Egyptian decan-list disagreement here — Senenmut omits, Dendera includes a Sopdet-related entry. Caveat below.
decans.caveat: Egyptian decan-25 name varies across primary attestations.

western.picatrix_image: A woman weeping, dressed in linen; significations: sorrow, hard task, vehement labor.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix mourning-woman aligns with Nephthys (Egyptian mourning-goddess at the tomb of Osiris) — strong Hellenistic-Egyptian fusion.

western.picatrix_image: A man with monkey-features; significations: temperance, balance, contemplation.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix's 'monkey-featured man' is the baboon Thoth — preserved directly from Egyptian Hermes/Thoth imagery. The same two stars anchor the Manzil and Xiu — perfect alignment here.

western.picatrix_image: A man with a reed and a sickle, swarthy; significations: harvest, blackness, melancholy.

arabic_manzil.name: Baṭn al-Ḥūt / Al-Risha
arabic_manzil.translation: The Belly of the Fish / The Rope

decans.cross_tradition_notes: MANZIL CYCLE RESTART — Manzil 28 (Al-Risha) is the last of 28, closing the cycle. CHINESE XIU CYCLE — at Xiu-15 the palace shifts from Black Tortoise back toward White Tiger (which started at Xiu-15 in our anchoring; this is the natural cyclical structure).

western.picatrix_image: A man holding a book, dressed in green; significations: study, wisdom, secrets, hidden things.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: ALIGNMENT CAVEAT — Manazil (28-cycle) and Xiu (28-cycle) restart at decan 29 in our 36-decan framework. We list both the first and second occurrence; in software the spine should be aware of this cycle mismatch.
decans.caveat: Manzil/Xiu cycle iterates approximately every 28/36 decans; alignment here is conventional, not astronomical.

western.picatrix_image: A black man with a strung bow, ready; significations: lust, voracity, anger, violence.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Cycle continues. Dhaniṣṭhā 'wealth/drum' parallels Picatrix's vigorous archer.
decans.caveat: Manzil/Xiu cycle iteration as per decan 29.

western.picatrix_image: A prudent man with a peacock-feathered hat, holding a book; significations: thought, contemplation, knowledge.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Picatrix peacock-feather + book imagery preserves Greek-Egyptian Hermeticist iconography of Hermes Trismegistus.

western.picatrix_image: A man with a long beard, in green and red robes, royal; significations: rule, honor, but also forgetfulness.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Śatabhiṣā = '100 healers' — Varuṇa-water-as-medicine. Aquarius decan 2 in Picatrix matches the royal-physician archetype.

western.picatrix_image: A black man, with a strung bow, lascivious; significations: black work, but also love and conjunction.

vedic.symbol: front legs of funeral cot / two-faced man

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Pūrva-Bhādrapadā = 'former lucky-foot' — connects to Aja-Ekapad ('one-footed goat'), a cosmic-pillar deity. Cross-tradition: the one-legged Picatrix image of decan-2 returns here in a different valence.

western.picatrix_image: A man bearing a burden on his shoulders, dressed in white; significations: voyage, peregrination, journey.

vedic.symbol: rear legs of funeral cot / twin

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Pisces (the fish-pair) → cosmic-serpent (Ahirbudhnya) parallels. Egyptian decanic cycle closes with Khnum (ram), matching decan-1 ouroboros pattern.

western.picatrix_image: A man with a great body, with a beard, wearing white; significations: knowledge, theology, jurisprudence.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: Revatī ('wealthy') is the final nakshatra. Picatrix's bearded sage = Osiris in the Egyptian decan, completing the cycle.

western.picatrix_image: A young man, naked, holding a torch; significations: rest, ease, end and beginning, gathering of waters.

decans.cross_tradition_notes: CYCLE CLOSE — naked youth with torch (Picatrix) = Khepri (sunrise scarab, Egyptian renewal) = Pisces marking the end-and-beginning of the zodiac. Three traditions encode 'gathering of waters' here at the precessional dissolution-point.
